Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source was originally cited. Inflect's commercial data-centre directory (accessed Sep 2025 data) confirms Bujumbura has zero direct cloud on-ramps for AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, with traffic routed via Nairobi or further; official AWS and Google Cloud region listings confirm neither has any East African region, the nearest hyperscale presence being AWS Cape Town (South Africa) — consistent with connections of well over 100ms. PeeringDB shows only Akamai (a CDN, not a hyperscale/cloud compute provider) peering at the Burundi IXP, which does not meet the bar for local cloud presence. This triangulated evidence supports 'served remotely from distant regions only' — Value Code 2 is confirmed as the best available estimate; unchanged.
